newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says plans 97 Eurobonds, convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says plans 97 Eurobonds, convertible bonds.

text.p: Russian gas group Gazprom will issue Eurobonds and convertible bonds abroad this year but has no plans to issue new American Depositary Shares (ADS) in the near future, a senior Gazprom official said on Thursday.
"We have a programme and this year we plan to devote to the market of unsecured bonds and convertible bonds," said Gazprom board member responsible for securities Alexander Semenyaka.

"The convertible bonds will be convertible into shares from the nine percent share," he told a news conference. Foreign shareholdings in Gazprom are capped at nine percent of capital and about one percent of Gazprom is in foreign-trading ADS form.

ABN-Amro Bank said on Monday Gazprom had mandated it and U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs to put together a financing package and expected Gazprom would issue a Eurobond with a minimum size of $1 billion, and convertible bonds with a volume of $500 million to $1 billion, both within six months.
"Those are reasonable figures," Semenyaka said when quoted the figures for the Eurobond and convertible bonds. "Definite figure will be determined by demand."

He said that Gazprom's need for funds for long-term capital construction of gas pipelines, especially the Yamal project to Europe, meant that the company would not wait until the end of the year to issue the paper.
Gazprom signed a 1.68 billion mark credit from Deutsche Bank in Berlin on Wednesday to finance purchases of pipeline equipment from German manufacturers.

Gazprom owes the government about $2.5 billion, approximately the total of the ABN-Amro financing, which includes a bridge loan to be issued within a month worth $500 million to $1 billion, according to the bank.
